source.citation: D. Saad, J. Padova and Y. Marcus, Thermodynamics of mixed electrolyte solutions. XI. An isopiestic study of the quaternary system NaCl-KCl-CaCl2-H2O at 25 C, Journal of Solution Chemistry 9 (1980), 259-268.
source.pdf_kind: scanned page images with a publisher OCR text layer

locators.procedure: p.260 Section 2: stock solutions by weight, gravimetric chloride; NaCl and KCl treated as one pseudobinary salt NaCl.nKCl; NaCl isopiestic reference; I = 0.9-5.7 mol/kg at 25 C
locators.definitions: p.261: first column the NaCl reference molality m_r with the water activity in parentheses, both 'obtained from Hamer and Wu'; y_B = I_B/I = 3 m_B/(m_A + 3 m_B), m_A the total molality of the salt (NaCl.nKCl), m_B the CaCl2 molality; I the total ionic strength; phi_exp the observed mixture osmotic coefficient; phi(S) Scatchard-model values

transcription: Every value read from the rendered page images (300 dpi) and compared with the OCR text layer; the OCR reads Table II row 17 phi(S) as 't.190', printed 1.190. Values are kept as printed decimal strings.
composition: n is the KCl/NaCl amount ratio of the alkali salt; m_A = I (1 - y_B) is the total 1:1 molality, m_Na = m_A/(1 + n), m_K = n m_A/(1 + n), m_Ca = y_B I / 3, m_Cl = m_A + 2 m_Ca (formula molality per kg water).
isopiestic_relation: phi_exp q = 2 m_r phi_NaCl(m_r) with q = 2 m_A + 3 m_B = I (2 - y_B); phi_NaCl from Hamer and Wu 1972.
printed_inconsistencies: Table I row 1 (m_r 0.9834, y_B 0.2501): printed I = 1.1045 and phi_exp = 0.926 do not satisfy the isopiestic relation with the Hamer-Wu NaCl reference (it gives 0.952 from the printed I; I = 1.1345 would give 0.926).
Table I row 2 (m_r 0.9834, y_B 0.5002): the relation gives 0.926 against printed 0.931 (difference 0.005; other rows agree within 0.001).
Table III row 11 (m_r 2.7796, y_B 0.5003): printed phi_exp '10.32'; the relation gives 1.032 and phi(S) is 1.029.

The parenthesized water activities imply NaCl osmotic coefficients about 0.5% above Hamer-Wu at the same m_r, while phi_exp follows Hamer-Wu; the activities are retained as printed and are not an independent measurement.
uncertainty: No measurement uncertainty is stated for phi_exp; values are printed to 0.001. No pointwise sigma is inferred.
